newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa to talk to staff in pay row.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa to talk to staff in pay row.

text.p: German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG said on Monday it would continue to plead its case to employees in a lengthy pay dispute following the decision by one of its main unions to ballot for strike action.
"We shall continue to explain to our employees our point of view concerning the strategic and commercial future of the airline," a spokesman for Lufthansa said by telephone.

He said the airline was expecting to have to wait between four to six weeks before a final decision on strike action was taken and in that time would neither make changes to its service nor to the pay offer it has presented to workers.
Earlier, the DAG white collar union said it had decided to ballot workers on whether they were prepared to strike for a higher 1997 wage rise than that currently offered by Lufthansa.
The airline, which is seeking to reduce its costs in the face of growing competition in its domestic routes, has offered a 1.7 percent wage rise from April 1 this year, together with one-off bonuses.
DAG is seeking a wage rise in the region of four percent, and is unhappy that Lufthansa wants to tie staff to 27-month contracts.
It has already organised two limited walk-outs by air- and groundcrews that have cost the airline millions of marks in lost business.
